reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard binary package (-bin) that downloads prebuilt archives from the official Apifox domain (file-assets.apifox.com) with pinned SHA256 checksums. The only flagged issue (SUID on chrome-sandbox) is a well-documented requirement for Electron applications on Linux systems without user namespaces, not a malicious injection. Both qwen and deepseek correctly identified this as standard Electron packaging practice.
disagreement_analysis: openrouter/free flagged chmod 4755 on chrome-sandbox as a privilege escalation risk, claiming SUID 'should never' be enabled on Chromium sandbox binaries. This is factually incorrect - Electron's official documentation requires SUID on chrome-sandbox for the sandbox to function on many Linux distributions. This is standard practice across hundreds of Electron AUR packages (VS Code, Discord, Slack, etc.). The model confused an upstream application requirement with a malicious injection.

learnings: Models need better training on Electron packaging conventions - chmod 4755 on chrome-sandbox is a standard, documented requirement for Electron apps on Linux, not a security issue
The audit tool should recognize common Electron packaging patterns (chrome-sandbox SUID, bsdtar extraction of .deb files) as legitimate and not flag them
Free tier models (openrouter/free) may have weaker knowledge of Linux packaging conventions, leading to false positives on standard patterns
Tool errors (403, 429) should be handled gracefully without counting toward verdict agreement
